newsitem.title: UK: Saudi dissident hits back against wife's charges.
newsitem.headline: Saudi dissident hits back against wife's charges.

text.p: London-based Saudi dissident Mohammed Al Masari on Wednesday dimissed allegations he was breaching the terms of his permission to stay in Britain, saying they were part of an orchestrated campaign against him by the Saudi authorities.

Masari, whose fax campaign against the Saudi royal family strained relations between Riyadh and London last year, said allegations reported in the British and Arab press by his estranged wife were "a piece of fiction".

"The pattern of coverage is believed to be fuelled by the Saudi embassy...which is part of an ongoing campaign to discredit the leader of the only recognised Saudi opposition group," he said in a statement.
Britain last year tried to deport Masari after his campaign against the Saudi royal family so irked Riyadh that it threatened to pull out of lucrative weapons contracts with British firms.
But Masari, a former physics professor, was granted leave to stay in Britain by an immigration appeals tribunal.
His estranged American-born wife Lujan Nur Al-Iman has claimed in recent newspaper reports that Masari is keeping his sister Suha at his London home although her visa expired in March last year.
She also said Masari was claiming state aid in Britain for one of his sons who lives in Saudi Arabia.

Masari, who acknowledged earlier this month that he was financially broke and living on state welfare handouts, said his permission to stay in Britain included the right of abode for his immediate family.
"References to the harbouring of an illegal immigrant are completely unfounded...The issue of sister Suha's presence here is not in question," he said.
Britain's Home Office (interior ministry) said Masari's permission to stay in the country extended to his wife and young children.
